title: DyadMem: A Long-Term Memory Benchmark of How Agents Work with Users

object.carrier: Per-episode numbered memory bank of six typed atomic entries (user_profile, fact, episodic, agent_identity, agent_method, agent_knowledge), maintained chronologically across multi-session user-agent dialogues via gold state transition B_t* = Dedup([(B_{t-1}* ∪ C_t*) \ L_t*] ∪ A_t*). Dual-domain: user-side memory (user_profile, fact), shared episodic memory, and User-conditioned Relational Agent Memory (URAM: agent_identity, agent_method, agent_knowledge) recording how this particular agent should work with this particular user.

safety_property.statement: One memory-integrity property is operationalized, with no adversary: Update deletions should remove only entries that gold annotation marks superseded or explicitly terminated ('A superseded memory entry produces a deletion and a replacement addition, an explicitly terminated entry produces only a deletion'). Incorrect deletion of still-valid entries is named 'unsafe deletion' by the authors and reported as a first-class failure (62.55%-98.51% of predicted deletions are incorrect across the 20 models, Table 8) because deletion errors propagate to all future bank states. There is no privacy/authority dimension: unauthorized use of user memory, cross-user isolation, and adversarial corruption of the bank are not evaluated; all observed failures are benign-condition capability failures.
safety_property.operationalized_as: unsafe-deletion rate = FP_delete/(TP_delete+FP_delete) on gold-conditioned standalone Update (Appendix I.3), per model in Table 8 and averaged in 4.2 (84.1% open-weight / 78.1% proprietary); denominator is the model's own predicted-deletion count

assumptions: All 61,210 QA instances are answerable from a non-empty gold support set; any refusal is over-abstention and there is no gold refusal class
Offline chronological replay of fully synthetic multi-session dialogues with explicit temporal anchors; no live users, no interactive environment, no attack surface

Cross-model comparability enforced by fixed prompts, GPT-5-mini judge (calibrated vs 5 human annotators, kappa=0.7099), BGE-M3/NLI matcher, and identical failure handling (truncated/failed outputs stay in the denominator)
not_covered: No adversarial scenarios: no memory poisoning or injection, no prompt injection through stored content, no memory exfiltration
No cross-user boundary: whether an agent may reuse memory across users or leak one user's memory to another is out of scope
No attack-induced corruption: unsafe deletion and under-capture are self-inflicted model errors under benign conditions, not attack outcomes; no defense mechanism is proposed or evaluated

intervention.name: DyadMem benchmark and URAM formalization (dual-domain, full-pipeline memory evaluation)
intervention.description: Formalizes long-term agent memory as a gold state transition over six typed entry classes and decomposes the lifecycle into separately supervised stages (session-level Capture; gold-conditioned standalone Update with Add/Delete op-F1; query-level Recall against the terminal gold bank), plus two QA settings - Gold-Memory (gold support supplied) and Full-Pipeline (model-built bank, Recall up to K=16) - whose difference (Gold-to-Pipeline gap) quantifies end-to-end loss, with a controlled URAM-vs-Agent-only protocol on 500 episodes. For the survey this card supplies attack-free baseline evidence that frontier models systematically under-capture, mis-update (unsafe deletions), and incompletely retrieve user-side and relationship-specific memory; it proposes no defense.

controls.name: 20-model main comparison (16 open-weight + 4 proprietary) under fixed prompts, judge, matcher, embedding
Gold-Memory QA vs Full-Pipeline QA on the same question set (Gold-to-Pipeline gap)
URAM vs Agent-only paired variants on the same 500 episodes, scored against the same gold agent-side targets
DyadMem-Simple balanced 300-episode subset for three-judge comparison and human calibration

results.claim: DyadMem is a large-scale dual-domain long-term memory benchmark: 3,065 episodes, 50,961 sessions and 61,210 QA instances over 5 major domains and 25 subdomains, with 6 memory categories jointly annotated on the same trajectories
results.setting: synthetic multi-session user-agent dialogues (GPT-5.4 generation, plan-guided dialogue-first construction, 9 full-time QC annotators, 76.6% retention); 6 entry types: user_profile, fact, episodic, agent_identity, agent_method, agent_knowledge
results.quote: It contains 3,065 episodes, 50,961 sessions, and 61,210 QA instances across 5 major domains and 25 subdomains.

results.claim: On DyadMem, Gold-Memory QA is consistently strong (78.7%-96.3% across 20 models) but Full-Pipeline QA collapses to 47.7% average for open-weight and 57.4% for proprietary models - final-answer evaluation over long histories hides the loss introduced by the memory pipeline itself
results.setting: 20 frontier LLMs (16 open-weight + 4 proprietary), full DyadMem (3,065 episodes, 61,210 QA), Full-Pipeline = model-built bank with Recall up to K=16, judge GPT-5-mini, matcher BGE-M3+NLI
results.quote: Gold-Memory QA ranges from 78.7% to 96.3%, whereas Full-Pipeline QA averages 47.7% for open-weight models and 57.4% for proprietary models.

denominator.how_counted: Full benchmark QA denominator = 61,210 QA instances (Table 4 caption partitions 30,468+30,742); Grounded accuracy and over-abstention 'use all questions as their denominator'; truncated/empty/failed outputs remain in the denominator (3.3, I.5)

results.claim: The Gold-to-Pipeline gap (Gold-Memory accuracy minus Full-Pipeline accuracy) is 42.9 points for open-weight and 33.9 points for proprietary models - an end-to-end measure, explicitly not a causal allocation to stages
results.setting: same question set under the two QA settings; 20 models on full DyadMem; open-weight avg vs proprietary avg
results.quote: The resulting Gold-to-Pipeline gaps are 42.9 and 33.9 points for the two groups.

denominator.how_counted: Full benchmark QA denominator = 61,210 QA instances (Table 4 caption partitions 30,468+30,742); Grounded accuracy and over-abstention 'use all questions as their denominator'; truncated/empty/failed outputs remain in the denominator (3.3, I.5)

results.claim: Even the best model shows final QA can stay high while the memory bank is incomplete, unstable, or bypassed: Kimi-K3 reaches 74.9% Full-Pipeline despite 18.6% Capture recall and 31.7% Update op-F1; its 95.0% Gold-Memory score yields a 20.1-point Gold-to-Pipeline gap

results.claim: Capture is precision-heavy and recall-poor: open-weight models average 54.0% precision but only 15.1% recall; terminal banks hold about 75 entries at the median vs 323.6 in the gold bank (size ratios usually 0.20-0.35) - systematic under-extraction, not indiscriminate storage
results.setting: 16 open-weight models on full DyadMem; micro-averaged coverage matching (BGE-M3 0.82/0.67 + NLI adjudication) over session-level gold Capture entries
results.quote: Capture is precision-heavy and recall-poor: open-weight models average 54.0% precision but only 15.1% recall. The resulting terminal banks are also small, about 75 entries at the median, compared with 323.6 in the gold bank, and model-to-gold size ratios usually lie between 0.20 and 0.35.

results.claim: Gold-conditioned standalone Update averages only 18.6% op-F1 for open-weight and 24.5% for proprietary models, isolating memory maintenance from upstream errors
results.setting: model receives current dialogue + gold prior bank + gold Capture entries; op-F1 = macro-average of Add F1 and Delete F1 (index-matched deletions, coverage-matched additions)
results.quote: Gold-conditioned standalone Update averages 18.6% op-F1 for open-weight models and 24.5% for proprietary models.

denominator.how_counted: Update 'is evaluated on the 20,590 sessions containing at least one gold Add or Delete operation, no-change sessions are excluded from this score' (3.3; also G.3/I.3)

results.claim: Deletions are unsafe at scale: the unsafe-deletion rate (fraction of predicted deletions that are incorrect) averages 84.1% for open-weight and 78.1% for proprietary models; because deletion changes future bank contents, low precision here propagates beyond the current session
results.setting: gold-conditioned standalone Update on full DyadMem; per-model rates 62.55%-98.51% (Table 8); larger models are not consistently better
results.quote: Scale does not resolve the problem: larger models are not consistently better, and the unsafe-deletion rate, the fraction of predicted deletions that are incorrect, averages 84.1% and 78.1% for the two groups (Table 8 and Figure 5).

denominator.how_counted: I.3: rate = FP_delete/(TP_delete+FP_delete); 'The denominator is the number of predicted deletions' (model-specific, no fixed n stated)

results.claim: Retrieval finds single entries easily but support sets incompletely: leading models retrieve at least one gold entry at rank one on 85-89% of questions (Hit@1), yet Recall@n stays below 63% - assembling the complete support set is substantially harder
results.setting: terminal gold bank, ordered retrieval up to 16 indices, exact index matching; leading models = Kimi-K3, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4-Pro (Hit@1 88.8%/87.8%/87.8%, H.3)
results.quote: Leading models retrieve at least one gold entry at rank one on 85–89% of questions, yet their Recall@nn remains below 63%.

denominator.how_counted: Hit@1 is the fraction of questions whose first retrieved entry is gold (3.3); scored per question on the full benchmark; every question has non-empty gold support so empty retrieval is a failure (I.4)

results.claim: Jointly incorporating user-side memory and URAM beats general agent memory alone: positive controlled Update difference on all 20 models, QA difference positive for 17 of 20, mean QA gains +3.2 (open-weight) / +3.7 (proprietary) points, largest DeepSeek-V4-Pro +9.8
results.metric: paired delta of controlled URAM vs Agent-only (Update op-F1 and Full-Pipeline QA)
results.value: Update positive 20/20 models; QA mean gain +3.2 / +3.7 points; QA positive 17/20
results.setting: 500 paired episodes (DyadMem-Agent), both variants read the same sessions; QA on 1,735 URAM-only questions from each variant's own terminal bank; agent-side gold Add/Delete targets; semantic matching
results.quote: In Table 3, the results show positive effects on all 20 models on the Update task. The primary QA difference is positive for 17 models; the mean gains are +3.2+3.2 points for open-weight models and +3.7+3.7 for proprietary models. DeepSeek-V4-Pro gains the most at +9.8+9.8 points.

denominator.how_counted: QA difference on the 1,735 questions whose gold support contains only URAM entries (H.1, I.6); Update difference pooled per episode over evaluated sessions (H.4)

results.claim: The controlled URAM effect is concrete per model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro moves from 58.9% to 68.7% QA (abstention 26.0% -> 21.7%) and Qwen3.5-9B from 54.3% to 61.5% (abstention unchanged 8.6%); paired Update CIs include zero only for GLM-5.2, Kimi-K3, GPT-5.6-Sol
results.metric: pre/post Full-Pipeline QA under URAM vs Agent-only (H.4)
results.setting: same 500-episode controlled protocol; negative QA point estimates only for Llama-3.1-8B (-3.3), Qwen3-4B (-3.2), Qwen3-30B-A3B (-1.6), all with falling abstention
results.quote: DeepSeek-V4-Pro instead moves from 58.9% to 68.7% QA while abstention falls from 26.0% to 21.7%; Qwen3.5-9B moves from 54.3% to 61.5% with abstention unchanged at 8.6%.

denominator.how_counted: 1,735 URAM-only questions per variant; question-level paired bootstrap for QA CIs (H.4, I.6)

results.claim: User-side memory is harder to use end-to-end than agent-side: open-weight Full-Pipeline QA differs by 14.8 points between partitions while Capture and Recall differ by only 3.4 / 0.9 points; proprietary mean QA 51.0% user-centric vs 63.6% agent-centric - the difficulty lies in using user-side evidence after the stages are composed
results.metric: Full-Pipeline QA gap, user-centric vs agent-centric partitions
results.setting: 1,532 user-centric episodes / 30,468 questions and 1,533 agent-centric episodes / 30,742 questions; 20 models, Table 4
results.quote: Table 4 shows that open-weight Full-Pipeline QA differs by 14.8 points between the two sides, while Capture and Recall differ by only 3.4 and 0.9 points. Proprietary models show the same direction, with mean QA of 51.0% on user-centric questions and 63.6% on agent-centric questions.

denominator.how_counted: Table 4 caption: 'User-centric n=30,468; agent-centric n=30,742' (3,065 episodes, 61,210 QA instances)

results.claim: Memory type, not life domain, sets Capture difficulty: mean Capture F1 is about 50% for agent_identity and agent_method, 25% for fact, 16% for shared episodic memory, while across the five life domains Capture F1 spans only 22.7-26.3% - models capture explicit reusable agent-side rules far better than heterogeneous factual/episodic content
results.metric: mean Capture F1 by memory type and by life domain
results.value: about 50% agent_identity / 50% agent_method / 25% fact / 16% episodic; domains 22.7-26.3%
results.setting: 20 models averaged, per-type and per-domain breakdowns (Figures 7-8); Interpersonal & Communication lowest at 22.7% yet retains 50.1% Full-Pipeline QA
results.quote: Across the 20 models, Figure 7 shows that mean Capture F1 is about 50% for agent_identity and agent_method, 25% for fact, and 16% for shared episodic memory. By contrast, Figure 8 shows that capture F1 spans only 22.7–26.3% across the five life domains.

results.claim: The GPT-5-mini judge is reliable for QA scoring: on 5,935 DyadMem-Simple outputs with paired labels from five human annotators it reaches 86.52% agreement with Cohen's kappa 0.7099 and nearly symmetric FP/FN rates
results.metric: LLM judge vs human agreement (accuracy / kappa)
results.setting: DyadMem-Simple Full-Pipeline QA outputs (300 episodes / 5,935 QA), semantic-consistency decision, human = gold, 5 selected annotators; Table 5 confusion matrix TP/FP/FN/TN = 1,779/403/397/3,356
results.quote: Five selected annotators provide paired human labels for 5,935 outputs. Table 5 shows 86.52% agreement and Cohen’s κ=0.7099\kappa=0.7099 [6], while false-positive and false-negative rates are nearly symmetric.

denominator.how_counted: Table 5: 'LLM-human agreement on DyadMem-Simple Full-Pipeline QA (n=5,935)'; column totals 2,176+3,759 = 5,935

results.claim: Model rankings are judge-robust: under three judges (GPT-5-mini, Gemini-2.5-Flash, Claude-Haiku-4.5) the same top seven models are identified, no model moves more than three positions, and all pairwise Spearman correlations of the 20-model ranks are at least 0.988
results.setting: Full-Pipeline QA on DyadMem-Simple (5,935 QA) re-scored by three judges, 20 models, Table 11 underlying data
results.quote: Figure 3 shows a nearly unchanged model ordering across the three judges: they identify the same top seven models, no model moves by more than three positions, and all pairwise Spearman correlations [36] are at least 0.988.

results.claim: Answering style reverses Full-Pipeline rankings: Qwen3-4B scores 43.6% on Full-Pipeline QA, above the stronger Qwen3.5-9B at 38.1%, although Qwen3.5-9B wins on every upstream stage - the headline metric alone misleads
results.comparison: Qwen3-4B 43.6% > Qwen3.5-9B 38.1% on Full-Pipeline despite losing on Capture/Recall/Update/Gold-Memory
results.setting: full DyadMem, 20 models; reversal appears in both QA-target partitions and all five life domains; over-abstention ranges 9.2%-59.9% across models
results.quote: Qwen3-4B scores 43.6% on Full-Pipeline QA, above Qwen3.5-9B at 38.1%, although Qwen3.5-9B is stronger on Capture, Recall, gold-conditioned standalone Update, and Gold-Memory QA.

results.claim: The reversal tracks answering styles: Qwen3-4B has 16.2% over-abstention and 27.4% ungrounded-correct, whereas Qwen3.5-9B has 43.1% over-abstention and 10.3% ungrounded-correct; when correctness additionally requires retrieved support, Qwen3.5-9B leads 34.2% to 31.7% in Grounded accuracy - Full-Pipeline QA must be read jointly with Grounded/OA/Ung.

results.claim: Stronger retrieval only partly compensates a bad bank: on each model's self-constructed bank the best fixed reranker track improves QA for four of the five tested models, and stronger retrieval 'can recover part, but not all, of the end-to-end loss caused by an incomplete constructed bank'
results.metric: Full-Pipeline QA under external reranker tracks vs model's own selection
results.value: best fixed track improves QA for four of the five models
results.setting: five small models (Qwen3-4B/8B, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.8-27B, Llama-3.1-8B); tracks = BGE-M3 dense, bge-reranker-base/large/v2-m3 re-scoring top-30 of top-50 dense candidates, answer generation receives at most 16 memories; Table 10
results.quote: On each model’s self-constructed bank, the best fixed retrieval track improves QA for four of the five models; Qwen3.8-27B instead performs best with its own selection. These results show that stronger retrieval can recover part, but not all, of the end-to-end loss caused by an incomplete constructed bank.
